clues.text: This city is in the north-west part of Mexico. Its state is Sonora, a land in that same far corner.
clues.narrowing: rules out everything outside northwestern Mexico

source.quote: is the capital and largest city of the northwestern Mexican state of Sonora

clues.text: Summer heat here has hit almost 50 degrees. That makes it one of the hottest cities in the whole country.
clues.narrowing: rules out all but the hottest desert parts of Mexico

source.quote: Temperatures have been as high as 49.5 °C (121.1 °F) in the summer months, making it one of the hottest cities in the country.

clues.text: In the past, folks here used a much shorter name: Pitic. Two long old names both ended with that word.
clues.narrowing: rules out Mexican cities never known by the old name Pitic

source.quote: formerly called Pitic (as in Santísima Trinidad del Pitic and Presidio del Pitic)

clues.text: Cars are the main thing made in this city. Its car plants have led its growth since the 1980s.
clues.narrowing: rules out northwestern Mexican cities whose main industry is not car making

source.quote: The major manufacturing sector has been the production of automobiles since the 1980s.

clues.text: This is the capital city of Sonora. It is also the largest city in that state.
clues.narrowing: confirms the capital and largest city of Sonora

source.quote: is the capital and largest city of the northwestern Mexican state of Sonora
